correctness.rationale: Marker-free subsystem equals the Sturmian aperiodic shift. Counting length-m configurations with k markers by distinguished marker gives P_m=(m/k)[z^m]F^k summed over k, without primitive-period assumptions, yielding exact zeta. Rational equivalence uses eventual linear recurrences and Skolem–Mahler–Lech; Pólya–Carlson plus the identity F=1-1/zeta proves meromorphic natural boundary at the unit circle. Intersection with the marker-free finite-type symbol restriction rules out soficity. All 40 finite checks agree but are not relied on for infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Direct full-text comparison of the motivating (S,w)-gap paper and two closest completed zeta studies identified neither this Sturmian periodic-point formula nor the all-S rationality/natural-boundary equivalence. Binary S-gap shifts have different marker-free periodic components; finite-graph S-graph shifts do not cover arbitrary Sturmian factor languages. Seven published-finding corpus semantic queries and web variants returned only different settings. Inaccessible full text of a 2011 finite-code renewal paper remains a genuine historical-priority risk, but its abstract concerns finitely generated code sets rather than the arbitrary infinite decorated family.
